The EJR axiom requires that any group of s voters cohesive on at least ℓ candidates must have at least one member who approves ℓ members of W. With n=10 and k=5 the thresholds are s≥2ℓ.

Voters 1-3+8-10 (size 6) are jointly cohesive on the three x-candidates. The ℓ=2 threshold therefore forces |W∩{x1,x2,x3}|≥2; the ℓ=3 threshold forces |W∩{x1,x2,x3}|≥3. Consequently every EJR committee contains all three x-candidates.

Voters 4-7 (size 4) are jointly cohesive on {y4,y5,y6}. The ℓ=2 threshold therefore forces |W∩{y4,y5,y6}|≥2. Because |W|=5 and three x-candidates are already required, W must be exactly {x1,x2,x3,y4,y5} (or any two of the three y-candidates).  

Voter 1 approves precisely the three x-candidates inside this set, so |W∩A1|=3 for every EJR committee. Hence both the minimum and the maximum are 3 (choice E).

(The remaining candidates y1,z3, etc. cannot enter W without violating either the size constraint or one of the two cohesive-group conditions above.)

Final answer: E. min 3, max 3
public_text.14: After analyzing the approval sets and the requirements of EJR for a committee of size 5, I conclude that any EJR-satisfying committee must include at least two candidates from voter 1's ballot (to properly represent the large cohesive group of voters 1-3-8-9-10 who all approve the x's) but can include up to four (for instance by adding y1 along with three of the x's while still allocating the fifth seat to satisfy the disjoint group of voters 4-7). This rules out both extremes of 0-1 and 5, so the range is min 2, max 4.

Hence voter 1 obtains at most three representatives.  

An explicit EJR committee realizing the lower bound is {x1,x2,z1,y4,y5}; one realizing the upper bound is {x1,x2,x3,y4,y5}.  

H. min 2, max 3

Because voter 1 approves every x-candidate, this already forces |W ∩ A1| ≥ 2.

- {x1,x2,y4,y5,z1} (intersection size exactly 2) and

Both satisfy every cohesive-group witness. No feasible committee yields 0, 1, 4 or 5; constructions that attempt to reach 4 (by substituting z1 for one y-seat and adding y1) leave the 4-voter group with only a single approved winner, violating EJR.  

Hence the attainable interval is exactly {2,3} (choice H).
